atoms.text: This guide describes a bucket policy statement that lets the QuerySpan SQL engine read raw event files and write query results in a bucket named example-analytics-lake. The statement names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/QuerySpanExecutionRole in its Principal element, and the QuerySpan workgroup assumes that role when it runs queries. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-lake/raw-events/* so the engine can scan input partitions. It allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to raw-events/*, so the engine can enumerate partitions. It also allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-lake/query-results/*, where result files and metadata are written. The role must also carry an identity-based IAM policy with the same actions, because the bucket policy alone does not grant access to a principal in the same account unless the role is named explicitly, as it is here. Trust for the role is configured separately in its trust policy, and only the QuerySpan workgroup should be listed there. After you save the policy, run a test query that selects from a raw-events table and confirm that an output object appears under query-results/.

This guide describes a bucket policy statement that lets the QuerySpan SQL engine read raw event files and write query results in a bucket named example-analytics-lake. The statement names the service principal queryspan.amazonaws.com in its Principal element, so the engine calls the bucket under its own service identity. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-lake/raw-events/* so the engine can scan input partitions. It allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted by an s3:prefix condition to raw-events/*, so the engine can enumerate partitions. It also allows s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::example-analytics-lake/query-results/*, where result files and metadata are written. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition set to 111122223333 and an aws:SourceArn condition matching arn:aws:queryspan:us-east-1:111122223333:workgroup/*, so that only workgroups in your account can use this grant. Without these conditions, a workgroup owned by another customer could cause the service to act on your bucket. After you save the policy, run a test query that selects from a raw-events table and confirm that an output object appears under query-results/.

This guide covers a bucket policy statement for BatchLoom, a batch transformation service that reads landing-zone CSV files and writes transformed Parquet output. The bucket is named example-landing-and-curated, and the nightly job reads from the landing/ prefix and writes to the curated/ prefix. The Principal element names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/BatchLoomJobRole, which each job run assumes. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::example-landing-and-curated/landing/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-landing-and-curated/curated/*, and it requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal aws:kms. The statement also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the job can discover new input files by key. Because the role lives in account 444455556666, which differs from the bucket owner account, the role's own IAM policy must allow the same actions. Verify the setup by starting a manual job run and checking that curated/ contains Parquet files with the expected KMS encryption metadata.

This guide covers a bucket policy statement for BatchLoom, a batch transformation service that reads landing-zone CSV files and writes transformed Parquet output. The bucket is named example-landing-and-curated, and the nightly job reads from the landing/ prefix and writes to the curated/ prefix. The Principal element names the service principal batchloom.amazonaws.com, which the service uses when it runs jobs. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:GetObjectVersion on arn:aws:s3:::example-landing-and-curated/landing/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-landing-and-curated/curated/*, and it requires the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption header to equal aws:kms. The statement also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN so the job can discover new input files by key. Because the principal is a service rather than an identity in your account, add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 444455556666 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:batchloom:eu-west-1:444455556666:job/nightly-*. Verify the setup by starting a manual job run and checking that curated/ contains Parquet files with the expected KMS encryption metadata.

This guide explains how to let RollupHub write daily aggregation results into a bucket that belongs to a different account from the one running the jobs. RollupHub reads hourly metric files from a source bucket and writes the daily rollups to a bucket named example-reporting-output, owned by account 777788889999. The bucket policy statement names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::222233334444:role/RollupHubWriterRole in its Principal element. It allows s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-reporting-output/daily-rollups/*. The statement carries an s3:x-amz-acl condition that requires the value bucket-owner-full-control, so the owning account controls every object written. It also allows s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN, which RollupHub checks before starting a write. The role in account 222233334444 needs a matching identity policy that allows the same write actions against the output bucket. To test, trigger a rollup for a single date and confirm that the object under daily-rollups/ is owned by account 777788889999.

This guide explains how to let RollupHub write daily aggregation results into a bucket that belongs to a different account from the one running the jobs. RollupHub reads hourly metric files from a source bucket and writes the daily rollups to a bucket named example-reporting-output, owned by account 777788889999. The bucket policy statement names the service principal rolluphub.amazonaws.com in its Principal element. It allows s3:PutObject and s3:PutObjectAcl on arn:aws:s3:::example-reporting-output/daily-rollups/*. The statement carries an s3:x-amz-acl condition that requires the value bucket-owner-full-control, so the owning account controls every object written. It also allows s3:GetBucketLocation on the bucket ARN, which RollupHub checks before starting a write. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 222233334444 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:rolluphub:us-west-2:222233334444:pipeline/*, which limits the grant to pipelines in the job-running account. To test, trigger a rollup for a single date and confirm that the object under daily-rollups/ is owned by account 777788889999.

This guide configures access for LogLens, a log analysis service that reads compressed access logs and writes search result exports. The bucket is named example-access-logs, with input logs under the logs/ prefix and exports under the exports/ prefix. The Principal element names the IAM user arn:aws:iam::555566667777:user/loglens-service-user, whose access keys are stored in the LogLens connector configuration. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-logs/logs/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of logs/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-logs/exports/*, which is where each saved search writes its CSV output. A Deny statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false should accompany this statement, so all access uses TLS. Rotate the user's access keys on a fixed schedule, and update the connector configuration after each rotation. To validate, run a saved search over one day of logs and confirm that a CSV file appears under exports/.

This guide configures access for LogLens, a log analysis service that reads compressed access logs and writes search result exports. The bucket is named example-access-logs, with input logs under the logs/ prefix and exports under the exports/ prefix. The Principal element names the service principal loglens.amazonaws.com, so no long-lived credentials need to be stored in the connector configuration. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-logs/logs/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of logs/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-access-logs/exports/*, which is where each saved search writes its CSV output. A Deny statement for requests where aws:SecureTransport is false should accompany this statement, so all access uses TLS. Scope the grant with an aws:SourceAccount condition of 555566667777 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:loglens:us-east-2:555566667777:workspace/*. To validate, run a saved search over one day of logs and confirm that a CSV file appears under exports/.

This guide describes a statement that lets FeatureForge, a feature extraction job service, read training images and metadata and write feature tables. The bucket is named example-ml-datasets, with inputs under the raw-images/ prefix and outputs under the feature-tables/ prefix. The Principal element lists the account root arn:aws:iam::888899990000:root, which delegates access to IAM identities inside that account. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ml-datasets/raw-images/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ml-datasets/feature-tables/*, and the job writes one Parquet file per input shard. An aws:PrincipalTag/team condition set to data-science limits the grant to identities in that account that carry the tag. The FeatureForge execution role in account 888899990000 must have this tag and an identity policy that permits the same actions. Test by running a job on a small shard and confirming that one Parquet file is written to feature-tables/.

This guide describes a statement that lets FeatureForge, a feature extraction job service, read training images and metadata and write feature tables. The bucket is named example-ml-datasets, with inputs under the raw-images/ prefix and outputs under the feature-tables/ prefix. The Principal element lists the service principal featureforge.amazonaws.com, which is the identity the service uses when its jobs run. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ml-datasets/raw-images/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ml-datasets/feature-tables/*, and the job writes one Parquet file per input shard. An aws:SourceArn condition matching arn:aws:featureforge:us-east-1:888899990000:job/* limits the grant to jobs created in your account. An aws:SourceAccount condition of 888899990000 is added alongside it, so the grant holds even if the ARN pattern is later broadened. Test by running a job on a small shard and confirming that one Parquet file is written to feature-tables/.

This guide covers ScanGrid, a data quality scanning service that reads files from a landing zone and writes validation reports. The bucket is named example-ingest-landing, with incoming files under the inbox/ prefix and reports under the dq-reports/ prefix. The Principal element names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::123412341234:role/ScanGridScannerRole, which the scan scheduler assumes at the start of each run. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-landing/inbox/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of inbox/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-landing/dq-reports/*, whereone JSON report is written per scanned file. Add an aws:SourceIp condition that lists the egress ranges of the network the role is used from, if your security policy requires it. Review the role's session duration, since long scans that outlast the session will fail partway through a write. Verify the configuration by placing a sample CSV in inbox/ and checking that a JSON report appears under dq-reports/.

This guide covers ScanGrid, a data quality scanning service that reads files from a landing zone and writes validation reports. The bucket is named example-ingest-landing, with incoming files under the inbox/ prefix and reports under the dq-reports/ prefix. The Principal element names the service principal scangrid.amazonaws.com, which the scan scheduler uses on every run. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-landing/inbox/* and s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of inbox/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-ingest-landing/dq-reports/*, where one JSON report is written per scanned file. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 123412341234 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:scangrid:us-east-1:123412341234:scan-policy/*, since the service calls come from its own endpoints rather than from your network ranges. Because the service holds no session of its own, session duration does not constrain long scans. Verify the configuration by placing a sample CSV in inbox/ and checking that a JSON report appears under dq-reports/.

This guide describes a bucket policy for TableMint, a service that compacts small input files into larger table files in a data lake. The bucket is named example-lake-tables, and compaction jobs read from the staging/ prefix and write compacted files to the tables/ prefix. The Principal element names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::303030303030:role/TableMintCompactionRole. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-tables/staging/*, because staged files are removed after a successful compaction. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-tables/tables/*. The statement also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted to the staging/ and tables/ prefixes through an s3:prefix condition. The role's identity policy should list the same actions, and its trust policy should name only the TableMint compaction scheduler. To verify, stage several small files, run a compaction, and confirm that one larger file exists under tables/ and the staged files are gone.

The Principal element names the service principal tablemint.amazonaws.com. The statement allows s3:GetObject and s3:DeleteObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-tables/staging/*, because staged files are removed after a successful compaction. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-lake-tables/tables/*. The statement also allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN, restricted to the staging/ and tables/ prefixes through an s3:prefix condition. Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 303030303030 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:tablemint:us-west-1:303030303030:compaction/*, so that only compaction tasks from your account can act on the bucket. To verify, stage several small files, run a compaction, and confirm that one larger file exists under tables/ and the staged files are gone.

This guide covers PipeCrunch, a scheduled job service that reads partner-supplied data files and writes enriched output into a shared bucket. The bucket is named example-partner-exchange, with partner files under the inbound/ prefix and enriched output under the enriched/ prefix. The Principal element names the IAM role arn:aws:iam::606060606060:role/PipeCrunchRunnerRole, which is the role assigned to the PipeCrunch job definition. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-partner-exchange/inbound/*, and it allows s3:ListBucket on the bucket ARN with an s3:prefix condition of inbound/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::example-partner-exchange/enriched/*, and each run writes one output object per input file. A separate Deny statement blocks s3:DeleteObject on both prefixes for every principal except this role, which keeps an audit trail of the data. Check the role's attached permission boundary, because a boundary that omits these actions overrides the bucket grant. Validate the setup by uploading a sample partner file and confirming that an enriched object with the same base name appears.

Add an aws:SourceAccount condition of 606060606060 and an aws:SourceArn condition of arn:aws:pipecrunch:us-east-1:606060606060:job-definition/partner-*. Validate the setup by uploading a sample partner file and confirming that an enriched object with the same base name appears.
